- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.

This project has no CONTRIBUTING.md. Write one explaining how to set the project up, how to run the tests, and what to do before opening a pull request.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Everything written into a file is in English, always, whatever language the request was written in. This covers documentation, comments, docstrings, identifiers and commit messages. Only the reply in conversation follows the language of the request.
- Markdown is soft-wrapped: one paragraph, one line. Never hard-wrap prose at a column limit, and do not copy the wrapping of the file you are editing. Rewrapping belongs to whatever renders the text, which is the only thing that knows the reader's width.

+# Contributing
+
+Thank you for your interest in contributing! This guide will help you get the project set up locally and understand our development workflow.
+
+## Project Setup
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- Python 3.8 or higher
+- pip (Python package manager)
+
+### Local Development
+
+1. Clone the repository and navigate to the project directory:
+```bash
+git clone <repository-url>
+cd <project-name>
+```
+
+2. Create a virtual environment:
+```bash
+python -m venv venv
+source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+```
+
+3. Install the project in development mode:
+```bash
+pip install -e .
+```
+
+If no setup.py or pyproject.toml exists yet, you may simply work with the Python files directly in your environment.
+
+## Running Tests
+
+Currently, the project does not have a formal test suite. Before opening a pull request, please:
+
+1. Verify your changes work correctly by testing them locally
+2. If adding new functionality, write tests using pytest
+3. Ensure all existing functions continue to work as expected
+
+To run tests once they are in place:
+```bash
+pytest
+```
+
+## Before Opening a Pull Request
+
+1. **Test your changes**: Run your code to verify functionality
+2. **Follow Python conventions**: Use PEP 8 style guidelines
+3. **Add docstrings**: Document function behavior with clear docstrings
+4. **Update documentation**: If your changes affect the README or add new functionality, update relevant docs
+5. **Write tests**: Include tests for any new code or bug fixes
+6. **Create a clear commit message**: Write descriptive commit messages explaining the "why" behind changes
+
+## Code Style
+
+- Follow [PEP 8](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/) for Python code
+- Use clear, descriptive variable and function names
+- Keep functions focused and modular
+- Add comments only when the logic is non-obvious
+
+## Questions?
+
+If you have questions about the project or need clarification on any part of this guide, feel free to open an issue or ask in the PR discussion.
